what: MEASURED 2026-09-22 by the R5 lane by re-running scripts/ops/build_strategy_evidence.py over the 40 legs R1 had not covered and diffing every record against its committed predecessor. POPULATION: the 30 legs that graded `measured` in both the committed run (2026-09-13/16) and this one (2026-09-22). RESULT: config_fingerprint is IDENTICAL on 40 of 40, so no config moved, and the cost code did not change in the window (git log --since=2026-09-10 over backtest_trend/pullback/squeeze + regime_debt_matrix = two commits, neither touching cost resolution) -- yet 2 of the 30 FLIPPED THE SIGN OF THEIR VERDICT on nothing but a 9-day shift of the rolling 365-day window. squeeze_breakout_4h: +0.5994 `pass` -> -0.4874 `fail` (n 9->10). trend_donchian_sol: -1.0697 `fail` -> +2.8045 `pass` (n 56->57). [!] WHY THIS IS A DEFECT AND NOT MERELY VARIANCE: window_days=365 is measured BACKWARD FROM THE RUN DATE, so the same leg with the same config is a different measurement every day, and nothing in the record says so -- a consumer reading decision_rule.verdict cannot tell a robust pass from one that read fail last week. RULE-D1-STAGE0-NET-OF-FULL-COST is a strict `net_r_oos > 0` test with no minimum-n and no interval, so a leg sitting near zero gets a crisp verdict out of what is, at these n, noise. squeeze_breakout_4h sits at n=10, exactly the producer's own MIN_TRADES_FOR_POOLED floor, and it is `execution: live`. [!] THIS IS NOT A REQUEST TO WIDEN OR LOWER THE BAR and must not be read as one -- the canonical rule against moving a floor to manufacture a verdict stands, and the fix runs the other way: make the instrument REPRODUCIBLE, and make `inside the noise band` a state the record can express, per CLAUDE-RULES-CANONICAL 'Collapsed states'. [!] IT BLOCKS ACTING ON THE TWO OPERATOR QUESTIONS THIS LANE ANSWERED: trend_donchian_sol_4h (+4.1648, n=34, down from +8.9882 nine days earlier) and htf_pullback_trend_2h (+2.7979, n=80) both pass, and neither should be promoted while the verdict that would authorize it moves this much.
